title: Export Conformance Guidance v2 - SIEM Connector Integration
content:
Purpose:
This working-playbook defines conformance guidance for exporting audit and telemetry evidence from Redwood’s control plane to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, Microsoft Sentinel). It focuses on: RBAC v2-aware field mapping, a stable audit-log schema, evidence automation triggers, connector behavior under backpressure, and a concrete onboarding checklist for customers and partner integrators.

Scope & audience:
- Audience: Security engineers, SRE, solutions engineers, partner integrators.
- Scope: Outbound export formats (HTTP, HEC, Syslog, EventHub/Kafka), minimal required fields, RBAC-linked metadata, retention/PII constraints, and test-validation recipes. Not covered: internal data-model changes unrelated to exports.

Key principles:
1) Deterministic schema: every exported event must include the canonical audit envelope (see sample below).
2) RBAC provenance: exports must carry role+principle mapping consistent with RBAC v2 so downstream SIEM correlations can attribute actions to policy grants.
3) Evidence packaging: small payloads preferred; large artifacts must be referenced with signed short-lived URLs and a manifest.
4) Graceful degradation: connector must queue locally and expose metrics when downstream sinks throttle.

Minimal audit envelope (compact example):
{
  "envelope_version": "1.1",
  "timestamp": "2024-03-10T14:12:23Z",
  "tenant_id": "org_12345",
  "resource": "/models/embedding-1",
  "action": "model.infer.request",
  "actor": {
    "principal_id": "user_678",
    "type": "user",
    "roles": ["app-developer", "audit-read"]
  },
  "rbac_grants": ["policy:serve:dedicated", "policy:read:billing"],
  "outcome": "success",
  "latency_ms": 58,
  "token_count": 42,
  "evidence_refs": ["evid_20240310_0001"]
}
Notes on fields:
- envelope_version: bump when incompatible changes are introduced. Consumers should ignore unknown fields by default.
- rbac_grants: contains canonical grant identifiers (not freeform role names) mapped from RBAC v2. See mapping section.
- evidence_refs: short ids; bulk artifacts are stored in object storage and referenced by signed URLs emitted in a separate evidence bundle export.

RBAC v2 -> SIEM mapping guidance:
- Map RBAC policies to two SIEM fields: rbac_grants (list of canonical ids) and effective_role (primary role inferred for quick alerts).
- When multiple policies apply, effective_role is the most-privileged grant by policy precedence table.
- Include policy_version to allow historical replay.

Connector behavior matrix (high level):
- Splunk HEC: support JSON envelope over HEC with grouping key tenant_id; prefer batching in 1s windows, max batch size 50 events. Backpressure: HEC 429 -> exponential backoff with jitter, local disk spool up to 5GB. Metrics: splunk_export_errors, splunk_backpressure_seconds.
- Datadog: use Logs intake with quality-of-service tagging (ddsource=redwood, service=inference-export). Use smaller batches (<=25) to avoid API limits. Respect rate limit headers; emit rate_limit_exceeded metric.
- Sentinel (EventHub/Azure Monitor): when using EventHub, ensure partition key = tenant_id for ordering. For Azure Monitor HTTP ingestion, include subscription and resource metadata. Support Azure-specific throttling headers and implement retry-after honor.

Evidence automation (attachment + automated bundling):
- Evidence types: (A) short text artifacts (included inline), (B) binary artifacts (logs, traces), (C) PII flagged snippets (sensitive).
- Automation rules: when an audit event matches a rule (alert severity >= medium OR outcome=failure with sensitive resource), create an evidence bundle. Bundle contains manifest JSON and signed presigned URLs with TTL default 7 days.
- Redaction policy: PII fields must be redacted before export unless customer explicitly enables full-evidence mode and provides a data processing agreement. Redaction should be recorded in the envelope with redaction_reason.

Throttling, backpressure, and loss modes:
- Local queue: in-memory ring buffer + disk spool. Configurable thresholds: mem_limit_events=5000, spool_limit_mb=5120.
- If spool full: apply oldest-first drop policy for non-failure informational events; preserve failure/audit-critical events above threshold. Emit metric export_queue_dropped_events with reasons.
- Failure handling modes: retry (default), spool-to-s3 (for later replay), controlled-drop on prolonged outage (alert on control plane).

Onboarding checklist (customer-facing):
1) Share target SIEM endpoint(s), ingestion method (HEC/HTTP/EventHub/Kafka), and any required auth tokens. (Jira: JIRA-SIEM-1284)
2) Provide tenant identifiers to be used as partition keys.
3) Agree on PII handling: redaction vs full-evidence. Sign DPA if required.
4) Validate sample events: we will send a 24-hour sample set of events containing success/failure/edge cases. Customer to confirm field mapping.
5) Acceptance tests: field presence test, RBAC provenance test, latency test (95p < 200ms), evidence retrieval test (signed URL TTL and access).

Testing recipes (quick):
- Field Presence Test: emit 100 events across three tenants; assert all events include envelope_version, tenant_id, actor.principal_id, rbac_grants, and evidence_refs.
- RBAC Repro Test: simulate role escalation and ensure effective_role changes and policy_version increments.
- Backpressure Simulation: temporarily return 429 from sink and assert connector backs off, spools to disk, and metrics increment.
- Evidence Bundle Retrieval: for three sample bundles, fetch signed URLs and verify object checksum.

Operational SLOs & alerts:
- Export success rate >= 99.5% over rolling 24h (exclude planned maintenance).
- Mean export latency < 250ms for direct HTTP paths.
- Alert: export_queue_size > 80% of spool_limit -> pager to oncall.

Privacy & compliance notes:
- Default retention for evidence references in SIEM is configurable by customer; Redwood will not retain signed URLs beyond bundle TTL without explicit config.
- For regulated customers, require Private deployment (control plane in-customer-network) or a version of the connector that omits signed URLs and pushes artifacts into the customer-controlled storage.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do Partners require a GCP Pub/Sub native path for Sentinel integrations? (action: Diego to confirm by 2024-03-17)
- Should evidence bundle TTL be adjustable per-tenant via Console? (action: Product to spec)

Appendix: quick sample scenarios and expected SIEM mapping (plain text)
- Scenario: failed model request with PII detection -> envelope outcome=failure, redaction_reason=pii-detected, evidence_refs=[evid_...] -> Connector creates evidence bundle, presigned_url TTL=7d, emits ddsource=redwood and a high-severity alert to Datadog.
- Scenario: rate-limited sink during deployment roll -> connector spools, emits splunk_backpressure_seconds and cluster-level alert, continues to serve requests with eventual replay.

This doc is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive. Use it as the engineering checklist for connector builds and customer onboarding. Update envelope_version when making breaking changes, and record those changes in the linked Confluence page.

Notes to reviewers: focus on compatibility gaps with current Splunk HEC implementation and whether our spool limits should be higher for large enterprise customers.
